newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank to consider rate rise in Jan - head.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank to consider rate rise in Jan - head.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland, the central bank, will consider if a rate rise is necessary to cool down credit growth after the release of inflation data for the whole of 1996, the NBP's president said.
Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told the Gazeta Wyborcza daily in an interview the central bank would be forced to raise interest rates if the current fast credit growth continues.

"If the fast credit growth continues, we will be forced to raise rates," she said. "For the time being I am warning. I think banks already believe the NBP's rates may rise. We shall see what inflation will be in 1996 and then decide," she said.

The Central Statistical Office (GUS) will release official data on consumer price growth in December and the whole of 1996 next month. In year-on-year terms it fell to 19.1 percent in November from 21.6 percent in december 1995.
The government expects the index to ease to between 17.9 and 18.2 percent in December while the NBP puts the figure at 18.6 percent.

Credit for households grew by almost 90 percent since the start of the year in nominal terms and corporate lending rose 31 percent while household deposits grew by 39 percent and corporate savings by 10 percent in that period.
However, in absolute numbers, credit for households rose by five billion zlotys while household deposits rose 15.4 billion.
Nominal credit for companies grew 15.7 billion zlotys in the first 11 months while corporate deposits rose 2.4 billion.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz said she hoped the potential rate rise would not slow the country's economic growth, seen at between 5.5 and 6.5 percent this year and next year, but said the bank's main concern was inflation.

"The aim of the NBP is not to hamper economic growth but our main goal is to curb inflation. Especially because it will not fall to the planned 17 percent this year, and the 13 percent target for 1997 seems unrealistic," she said.
